items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: So I joined Will Bradley for a guarantee of ninety dollars a week... I went to Nolas and sat in with the band, and they said well you’ve got the job if you want it.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about the first Herd, how that came about?

Well I was with the band — Teddy Powell had a band. And it was very similar as the First Herd in style. On that band was Buddy DeFranco on clarinet, and there was Boots Mussulli, and Charlie Ventura was on the band, and different guys, George Handy was writing charts for the band, and Eddie Finkel, the composer was writing charts. And it was pretty outside in a sense. And I joined the band. I remember being with the band about three or four months, and I got a call from two attorneys by the name of Vellum and…

rehearsing at Nola Studios in New York. And I don’t quite remember how I got there on a day off or something, but Ray McKinley or someone knew that I was interested and they said well we’re rehearsing at Nola’s and, when you can. So I went there and I sat in and they says, “The job is yours.” I think I was making about seventy dollars for the week with Sonny Dunham at the caverns or something. And it was a good band Sonny Dunham had, really, Uan Rasey was playing lead then, and he was just a kid himself. So I…

ctx.x: Yeah. Before the war, just before the war. And then like I said Carlos Gastel at one time, this was two years after, to me he said, “Hey kid, you want to join the band?” There was somebody by the name of Cohen who was a New York trumpet player, but before that, at Purdue, Will Bradley and Ray McKinley came in for one night to play for a dance and I subbed for one of the trumpet players. He was sick or something. I played the whole © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

night and I remember Ray McKinley, who was a wonderful guy, a great drummer really, and he had the boogie woogie band, you know with Freddie Slack, and I finished the gig and I was really excited. And I overheard Ray McKinley say, “You know when that kid gets some experience he’s going to be great.” Just like that. And I heard and I was insulted. I said what does he mean? I’m going to be great — I said I can do anything Harry does, which I used to do all the technical things Harry did. I says I can imitate Roy…
